subject: Inference billing models — post-demo recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T14:20:00Z
Subject: Inference billing models — post-demo recap & next steps

Sam — thanks for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a concreted ask so we can build the right pricing scenarios.

What we heard on the call (please confirm or correct):
- Expected steady-state volume: ~2.0B tokens / month (generation + embedding mix)
- Typical prompt + generation median length: ~512 tokens; p95 around 1,200 tokens
- Target 99th-pctl latency SLO: ~200ms for single-turn gen requests
- Sustained concurrent active requests: ~60–80; occasional peaks to ~140 for short windows
- Data residency: US only; SOC 2 evidence required for procurement

Three deployment paths you asked us to quantify: Hosted API (per-token), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), and Private VPC (customer-managed infra). I attached a simple cost workbook (Brightleaf_cost_model_v3.xlsx) but below are high-level ranges to set expectations. These are directional until Ben runs a sizing with exact model selection and quantization profiles.

1) Hosted API (fastest to launch)
- Unit model: per-token billing for generation + embeddings
- Ballpark: at 2B tokens/mo, hosted would be roughly $800k–$1.2M/mo depending on model family & streaming vs sync behavior (this range includes higher-cost long-form generation).
- Pros: no infra ops, immediate scaling; cons: unit costs highest, less control over tail latency.

2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Unit model: monthly reserved commit for a pool sized to your concurrency/throughput + overflow per-token pricing for bursts
- Ballpark: reserved commit starting ~$35k–$70k/mo for a baseline pool that covers your steady concurrency (approximate; depends on chosen model and batching). Expected unit economics per token can be 5–15x cheaper vs hosted once fully utilized.
- Pros: predictable cost, better tail latency control; cons: minimum commit and lead time to provision.

3) Private VPC / On‑prem (enterprise license)
- Unit model: platform license + ops support; CapEx/Opex for customer infra; Redwood offers a private control plane & optionally an on-prem package.
- Ballpark: typically multi-hundred-thousand USD/year in licensing + infra costs; attractive for sensitive data or very large sustained volumes when you can amortize hardware.

Requested next inputs from you so we can finalize a proposal:
- Confirm monthly token mix (gen vs embeddings) and a short sample of peak time windows (15–60m) so we can size the Dedicated pool correctly.
- Any mandatory compliance docs beyond SOC 2? (we attached our SOC 2 high-level questionnaire)
- Procurement contact and target procurement timeline (pilot -> pilot extension -> production recommended cadence)

Suggested immediate next step: a 6–8 week pilot on a small Dedicated pool (we recommend this for latency-sensitive apps) with a trial credit structure. If you confirm volumes and timeline I’ll put together a 1-page pilot SOW + a pricing table with three named scenarios (Fast Launch - Hosted, Predictable - Dedicated Pilot, Regulated - Private VPC).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m to lock scope tomorrow if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Brightleaf_cost_model_v3.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 1 sheet: scenario matrix)
Attachment: Brightleaf_SOC2_questionnaire_v1.pdf (PDF questionnaire)

From: Sam Torres <sam@brightleaf.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightleaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T17:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference billing models — post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Confirming the numbers on our side:
- 2.0B tokens/month is our best estimate for Q1 prod (30% gen, 70% embeddings by token count)
- Peaks: typically 30–45 minutes in the morning and after marketing campaigns; short spikes to ~150 concurrent for ~10 minutes
- Compliance: SOC 2 + a short runbook for access reviews; we can share a CDA if needed

Procurement timeline: we’d like a 90-day pilot to validate latency and cost. Procurement (procurement@brightleaf.ai) would need a short SOW + an outline of pilot terms to start approvals. Can Redwood table a Dedicated pilot proposal with an option to convert to a 6‑month reserved commit?

Also please flag any limits around KV cache persistence and whether prefix caching would be available for the Dedicated pilot — that will materially affect our token burn.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sam
Sam Torres
Product Lead, Brightleaf AI
sam@brightleaf.ai | +1 650-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Brightleaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference billing models — post-demo recap & next steps

Sam — thanks, that all helps. Deliverables attached and next steps below.

What we attached: 
- Brightleaf_cost_model_v3.xlsx: three rows for each scenario (Hosted / Dedicated Pilot / Private VPC) with token assumptions, expected GPU-hours equivalent, and a monthly cost range.
- Brightleaf_SOC2_questionnaire_v1.pdf: our responses to the standard SOC 2 checklist you referenced on the call.

Pilot proposal (summary):
- Duration: 90 days
- Environment: small Dedicated pool sized for steady-state ~60 concurrency, with burst overflow to Hosted tier
- Pilot commercial: $20k/mo reserved credit + discounted usage rates during pilot. Credit is applied against committed baseline; bursts billed per-token at a reduced hosted rate.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms, no functional regressions on your reference prompts, and total cost per 1M tokens <= target threshold (we’ll confirm after Ben runs the sizing).

Specific asks for procurement to include in SOW:
- Acceptance window and success metrics (as above)
- Contact for billing and PO issuance
- CDA/required contract terms (we can share a redlineable SOW)

Next steps I’ll take this week: Ben will run a model-specific sizing pass and update the workbook with per-model GPU-hour equivalents (this will give us a tighter committed amount). I’ll also draft the short SOW and pilot terms for procurement. Can procurement confirm the PO approver and whether they need a vendor risk assessment?

I’ll carve out 30m tomorrow afternoon to walk through the workbook if you’d like — please share a time.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: Brightleaf_cost_model_v3.xlsx (updated with scenario notes)
Attachment: Brightleaf_SOC2_questionnaire_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T16:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: Brightleaf pilot pricing recommendation (needs sizing + approval)

Ben/Rishi — internal note following Sam’s confirmation. Please keep internal.

Quick summary: Brightleaf (DEAL-4721) has ~2B tok/mo (30% gen /70% embeddings). They want a 90-day Dedicated pilot with an option to convert to 6-month reserved commit. Procurement expects an SOW and pilot commercial terms. I sketched a pilot commercial we can propose:
- Pilot: 90 days, $20k/month reserved credit (applied to baseline) + discounted burst rates (hosted) during pilot.
- Conversion offer: if they convert to min 6-mo commit within 30 days post-pilot, offer 12% credit back on pilot spend and a 10% discount on list committed price for first 6 months.

Action items:
- Ben: run the model-sizing pass (choose 2 candidate model families — one quantized Llama-style and one FP16 transformer) and output expected GPU-hours and recommended reserved pool size. Update Brightleaf_cost_model_v3.xlsx with a per-model line item. ETA 48 hours.
- Rishi: review the proposed commercial concession (12% pilot credit + 10% commit discount) and flag if we should cap the total concession per ARR, or change to a tiered discount based on committed throughput. Please approve or propose edits by EOD Wednesday.
- Marissa: I’ll draft SOW and basic acceptance criteria and send to Sam + procurement once Ben’s sizing is in.

Notes: make sure we call out KV/prefix caching behavior in the SOW (for Dedicated pilot we expose prefix caching for the test workspace; production caching policies can be tuned). Also prep a short table showing expected token burn reduction from prefix caching (we can put conservative 20–40% reduction range).

Thanks —
Marissa
